source: Letter-associates cross-reference — James's two circles: West Point + Co. I, 153rd NY
method: Read James's letters; extracted (a) his West Point/education associates and (b) his Co. I 153rd comrades; cross-referenced against verifiable West Point cadre and the 153rd roster. His military circle largely OVERLAPS brother Charles's (same Co. I) — overlap noted rather than re-derived; James-SPECIFIC associates flagged.

west_point_circle.name_as_written: Mr. Michie, 'the Cadet Lieut. of our company'
west_point_circle.record_match: Peter Smith Michie, USMA Class of 1863 (graduated 2nd; later professor & Brig. Gen.) — VERIFIED real West Point cadet officer of fall 1862.
west_point_circle.note: Decisive cross-binding evidence that James was genuinely at West Point.

west_point_circle.record_match: Rev. John W. French, USMA Chaplain & Professor of Ethics — VERIFIED.
west_point_circle.note: Gave the cadets prayer books; second independent West Point corroborator.
James-specific; Clinton County academy tutor who prepared him for the appointment ('studying under Everest will be a first rate thing'). Not in any military record.
Helped secure the appointment. Distinct from 'Camp Wheeler' (Ogdensburg) and Confederate Gen. Joseph Wheeler — three different Wheelers.

west_point_circle.name_as_written: young Hoyt; Mr. Holcomb; Dobbin (academy master)
west_point_circle.note: West Point peer / travel companion / pre-WP Champlain academy — education circle, honest nulls.

co_I_153rd_circle.verbatim_letter_context: 'Lucas was badly wounded. He is the only one you know in the company.'
co_I_153rd_circle.record_match: LUCAS, JAMES — Co. I; killed in action Oct 19 1864 at Cedar Creek (per the full roster).
co_I_153rd_circle.note: OVERLAP with Charles's circle. James reported him wounded; the record shows killed.

co_I_153rd_circle.verbatim_letter_context: 'Alex Douglas has been boggled by the guerrillas' (captured near Cedar Creek)
co_I_153rd_circle.record_match: DOUGLASS, ALEXANDER J. — Co. H→Co. I; commissary sergeant May 9 1864; survived, mustered out 1865.
co_I_153rd_circle.note: OVERLAP with Charles's circle; survived (feared captured).

co_I_153rd_circle.verbatim_letter_context: 'Did Lt. Colonel Strain lose a leg?'
co_I_153rd_circle.record_match: STRAIN, ALEXANDER — Capt. Co. G → Lt. Col.; wounded Cedar Creek; discharged for wounds Jan 1865, no amputation recorded.

co_I_153rd_circle.verbatim_letter_context: 'James Sweeney has lately come into our regt. as Surgeon... such a little faller when he left our place' (a hometown man)
co_I_153rd_circle.record_match: SWEENEY, JAMES — assistant surgeon, 153rd NY, mustered in June 1 1864; prior service captain 96th Infantry; survived.
co_I_153rd_circle.note: JAMES-SPECIFIC associate (a Champlain hometown connection) emphasized in James's letters more than Charles's.

shared_co_I_officers_overlap: Capt. Davis J. Rich, Capt. John F. McGuire, Lt. Charles L. Knapp, 1st Sgt Samuel Peltier — all confirmed Co. I (see PER-hubbell-charles/letter-associates-crossref.json); James's company circle is Charles's company circle (they served together in Co. I).

summary.james_specific_find: Asst. Surgeon James Sweeney (hometown connection); plus the entire West Point circle, which is unique to James among the four brothers.
summary.key_point: James is the only brother with TWO distinct social worlds in the record — the West Point cadet corps (Michie, French) and his brother's Co. I — and the cross-reference verifies a real figure in each.
